extra.explanation: A 5% risk-free return raises the bar for every other asset and raises financing costs, which hits borrowers like utilities, homebuilders and REITs most. A strong economy is not what the yield shows here, since inflation and policy expectations also drive it.
options: It shows the economy is growing faster than expected
Safe bonds now pay more, so riskier assets must offer higher returns and borrowing costs rise
It means companies have stopped paying dividends
It lowers oil prices and cuts energy profits
extra.prompt: The 10-year Treasury yield closed at about 5.00% on Friday. Why does a yield that high pressure stocks and real estate?

extra.explanation: Salesforce's marketing tools lagged newer rivals in real-time engagement, and buying Braze is quicker than rebuilding, though costly. The premium also reflects how few independent platforms of this kind exist.
options: It fills a product gap faster than building a new tool, and rival bidders could drive the price
It lets Salesforce exit the marketing business
It is mainly a way to cut headcount at Braze
It lowers Salesforce's tax bill
extra.prompt: Salesforce is paying a 58% premium to buy Braze. What is the main business logic?

extra.explanation: Revenue grew 9% and credit-loss provisions fell, so the business was healthy. The $336M restructuring charge and fears about service quality weighed on the shares even as guidance rose.
options: Credit losses had risen sharply
Strong revenue let it invest, while cost cuts aim to use AI to lower expenses; the restructuring charge worried investors short term
It lost cardholders to rivals
Interest rates had fallen
extra.prompt: American Express raised its profit outlook but announced a 5% job cut, and its stock fell 3.7%. What best explains the pairing?

extra.explanation: A 73/27 split means EQT shareholders keep clear control, so this is a larger company absorbing a smaller one. It is all stock, so no cash changes hands, which keeps the combined company's debt low.
options: The two companies are roughly equal partners in the new company
Range holders also receive a large cash payment on top of their shares
EQT is the larger partner, and its holders keep about 73% of the combined company
Range will be the controlling shareholder after the merger
extra.prompt: In the EQT and Range all-stock deal, Range holders get 0.987 EQT shares per share and end up with about 27% of the combined company. What does that split show?

extra.explanation: More customers, lower churn (0.87%) and a wider margin together point to growth that adds profit. A discount-led push would normally push the margin down, and capital spending guidance of $16.0B to $16.5B was unchanged.
options: It gave up profit to win customers through heavy promotions
Its growth came mainly from cutting prices across the board
It trimmed network spending to lift its margin
It is adding customers and keeping them, so growth is not simply being bought with discounts
extra.prompt: Verizon added 406,000 postpaid phone customers, up from 44,000 a year ago, while its EBITDA margin rose to 40.2% from 37.8%. What does this combination suggest?

extra.explanation: Nitrogen fertilizer uses natural gas as feedstock and fuel, so a gas price spike raises production costs and fertilizer prices. That in turn raises farmers' input costs.
options: Farmers burn gas to dry their crops
Gas is shipped in the same vessels as fertilizer
Fertilizer producers buy gas only from farmers
Fertilizer such as ammonia and urea is made from natural gas, so gas is a main input cost
extra.prompt: Why do fertilizer prices tend to rise when natural gas prices rise?

extra.explanation: Frontier AI development depends on huge compute spending, so raising capital in public markets is the main benefit. A listing adds disclosure obligations rather than removing them, and the valuation is set by investors, not guaranteed.
options: It removes the need to buy chips and cloud capacity
It guarantees a higher valuation than private rounds
It opens access to far more capital for compute spending, and exposes its economics to investors
It lets the company stop reporting financial results
extra.prompt: Anthropic filed an S-1 but has not set a price range. Why does a public listing matter most for an AI model developer?

extra.explanation: A price below net asset value, even with a 30.1% premium to the market price, shows MidCap traded at a discount to book. Larger lenders gain scale with over $31B of investments and 800+ portfolio companies. The deal is mostly stock, with about $1.21 per share in cash.
options: Business development companies cannot lend to mid-sized firms
Smaller lenders can trade below book value, so scale buyers can combine them
Ares Capital expects MidCap's loans to default
The deal will be paid entirely in cash
extra.prompt: Ares Capital is buying MidCap Financial, a smaller lender, at $10.88 per share against a reported NAV of about $12.86. What does this suggest?

extra.explanation: Care is moving to outpatient settings where procedures are cheaper and insurers prefer to send patients. Owning the network gives the system lower-cost capacity and surgeon relationships. The other options are wrong because surgery centers are paid by insurers and Medicare and do not rely on inpatient beds.
options: Surgery centers are mostly inpatient and need more beds
Surgery centers are paid by patients only, not insurers
Same-day procedures are cheaper to deliver outside hospitals, and the network ties surgeons to the system
The deal removes the need for any insurance contracts
extra.prompt: A nonprofit health system is buying Surgery Partners, which runs 200+ surgery centers, for about $5.7B. What is the main business logic?

extra.explanation: Appliance makers carry large fixed costs, so fewer units sold leave the same cost base to cover. Whirlpool's filing also points to tariff costs and inflation. Dividends are a payout of profit, not an operating expense.
options: Appliances are sold below cost in every quarter
Whirlpool cuts prices when sales rise
Fixed factory and distribution costs spread over fewer units, and tariffs and inflation add costs
Dividends are counted as an expense
extra.prompt: Whirlpool's sales fell 8.8% but ongoing EPS swung from a $2.09 profit to a $0.21 loss. Why does a sales decline hurt profit so much?

extra.explanation: Both dissenters wanted a quarter-point hike and futures priced about 85% odds of one in December, so the debate is about more tightening. Cuts and 'finished' do not fit those facts, and the Fed said inflation is too high.
options: Markets expect rate cuts early next year
The Fed has finished its policy changes for good
Markets expect further tightening, not near-term cuts
The Fed is worried about falling inflation
extra.prompt: The Fed held at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote, with both dissenters wanting a hike and futures pricing about an 85% chance of a December hike. What does this signal?

extra.explanation: A 53% rise in volume outweighed the 15% drop in realized price, giving 39% growth. One-time items were only about $900M of $24.4B, so they were not the main driver.
options: Prices rose in other regions
Lilly stopped paying rebates
Volume grew 53%, more than offsetting lower prices
One-time items made up most of the growth
extra.prompt: Lilly's revenue grew 39% while realized prices fell 15%. What made that possible?

extra.explanation: Volume added $2.2B and pricing $663M, which more than covered tariff-related costs. Power and Energy, which grew 18%, was the highest-margin segment, so lower power sales would not help.
options: Cutting prices to win share
Selling the construction division
Lower sales of power equipment
Higher volume (+$2.2B) and price realization (+$663M) outpacing tariff costs
extra.prompt: Caterpillar's operating margin rose to 20.4% from 17.3% on 17% sales growth. What mainly drove the improvement?

extra.explanation: AWS produced about 63% of operating income from under a quarter of sales. Trailing free cash flow was an outflow of $42.4B because capital spending ran at $215.2B over the year, so cloud is highly profitable but also the reason cash is draining.
options: Cloud is a small side business inside Amazon
AWS earns most of Amazon's profit, but heavy data center spending has pushed free cash flow negative
Retail now earns higher margins than cloud
Amazon has stopped building data centers
extra.prompt: AWS grew 39% to $46.0B and earned $17.8B of Amazon's $28.1B operating income, while Amazon plans about $220B of capex in 2026. What does this show?

extra.explanation: DoorDash cited scale in grocery delivery to lower fulfillment costs, plus advertising reach and Instacart's software for grocers. It is not a way around regulators: the close is not expected until the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028, after antitrust review.
options: Instacart's partner stores will be closed to cut costs
Combined order volume lowers fulfillment cost per order and strengthens the advertising and software offer
The deal lets DoorDash avoid antitrust review
It guarantees higher prices for every grocery shopper
extra.prompt: DoorDash will pay $65 per Instacart share, about $17B, and expects at least $500M of annual synergies. What is the main business logic?

questions.explanation: The October sell-off centered on AI-linked stocks: Alphabet had its worst day on record, Intel fell about 29% and a chip ETF lost more than 8% on Friday. The Dow holds fewer such companies, and money moved into health care and consumer staples.
options: Investors sold industrial and health care companies the most
Higher oil prices hurt technology companies through fuel costs
Doubts about returns on heavy AI spending hit the technology and chip stocks that dominate the Nasdaq
The Fed cut interest rates, which favors the largest banks
questions.prompt: The Nasdaq fell 5.3% in October while the Dow rose 1.7%. What best explains the gap?

questions.explanation: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15 to $16 billion, with earnings per share below consensus. Share prices reflect expected future profit, so a weak outlook can outweigh a strong quarter that has already happened.
options: Markets price the future, and a fourth-quarter forecast below consensus outweighed the good quarter
Investors were reacting only to a quarterly loss
Intel announced a large new share sale
Intel cut its dividend
questions.prompt: Intel beat third-quarter expectations, yet its shares fell about 29% on Friday. What does this show?

questions.explanation: Enterprise value is equity value plus net debt, so the $7.7 billion gap points to heavy borrowing. Recurring monitoring fees make that debt manageable, which is what makes ADT attractive to a buyer financed by Apollo funds.
options: ADT holds a large cash pile that Thrive will keep
ADT carries heavy debt, about $7.7B of obligations that come with the company
Thrive is paying part of the price in shares
Thrive must pay a fee to rival bidders
questions.prompt: Thrive's ADT deal values the equity at about $7.6B but the whole company at $15.3B. What does the gap mainly show?

questions.explanation: Farxiga and Brilinta lost exclusivity, so cheaper copies took sales, and China's volume-based procurement cut prices. This is the patent cliff: a company must grow new products, like its cancer drugs, faster than old ones shrink.
options: Weak demand for its rare disease drugs
Currency moves alone
New US price controls on all drugs
Patent expiries on Farxiga and Brilinta plus China's volume-based buying
questions.prompt: AstraZeneca's oncology sales rose 18% while its BioPharmaceuticals unit fell 2%. What mainly explains the decline?

questions.explanation: Franchisors earn royalties as a percentage of sales at restaurants that franchisees run, so higher comparable sales lift revenue without much extra cost. Net restaurant growth, not comparable sales, counts new openings.
options: They count how many new restaurants opened
They are set by fixed lease terms
Its royalties are a share of franchisee sales, so revenue rises with little added cost
It owns most restaurants and books all their costs
questions.prompt: Burger King US comparable sales rose 8.4% while Popeyes fell 1.8%. Why do comparable sales matter so much to a franchisor like Restaurant Brands?

questions.explanation: A small beat on top of 30% growth means analysts had already raised their numbers. Stocks then need a stronger outlook, not just good results, to rise, which is why even strong reports can lead to share price drops.
options: Growth is strong but expectations were already high, leaving little room for upside surprises
Analysts have underestimated profits by more than usual
Corporate profits are falling
Companies have stopped giving forecasts
questions.prompt: S&P 500 profits are on track to grow about 30%, yet companies are beating estimates by only 1.4% against a 7.5% five-year average. What does this suggest?

questions.explanation: Visa earns fees per payment, and cross-border payments carry extra fees, so faster growth there lifts revenue above domestic volume. Visa does not lend, as banks take the credit risk, and processed transactions rose 10%, not fell.
options: Visa raised interest rates on cardholders
Processed transactions fell 10%
Visa lends money directly to merchants
Cross-border volume grew 14% and carries higher fees than domestic payments
questions.prompt: Visa's revenue grew 13% in Q4 while payments volume grew 9%. What best explains the gap?

questions.explanation: An integrated company owns both production and refining. Upstream earned $7.1B, down on lower prices, while refining margins and strong diesel yields lifted Energy Products. A pure producer would not have that offset.
options: Refining and fuel margins can widen when crude prices ease, offsetting weaker production profits
Lower crude prices raise its output automatically
Governments pay refiners subsidies whenever crude falls
Its chemicals prices are fixed by ten-year contracts
questions.prompt: ExxonMobil's upstream earnings fell in Q3 2026 while Energy Products (refining) rose to $7.2B, lifting adjusted earnings to $17.5B. Why can an integrated oil company's profit hold up when crude eases?

questions.explanation: UPS is trading lower volume for better profit per package, cutting hours and buildings as Amazon deliveries leave. About $1.8B of a $3B savings target is already achieved, which is why margin rose as volume fell.
options: It raised prices on every customer by 10%
It deliberately shed low-margin Amazon volume and cut matching costs
It sold its delivery network
Fuel costs fell sharply this quarter
questions.prompt: UPS's US average daily volume fell 3.3%, yet its domestic margin rose 60 bps to 7.0%. What best explains this?

questions.explanation: The industry profile notes that costs are mostly fixed, so profit depends on how full flights are. IATA expects only about a 2% net margin in 2026, meaning a few empty seats can erase it.
options: Fuel is bought separately for each passenger
Governments set ticket prices below cost
Most costs, such as planes, crews and airport fees, are fixed per flight, so each extra passenger adds revenue with little added cost
Airlines pay sales commissions only on full flights
questions.prompt: Why does a small change in the share of seats filled swing an airline's profit so much?
